displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that finite consciousness modestly supports theism when divine mentality provides a unified personal ground for subjecthood, rational agency, and experiential intelligibility beyond merely locating consciousness among fundamental facts.

novelty.explanation: It repairs the conditional grounding claim by framing it as a modest comparative inference rather than a deduction from theoretical incompleteness.

premises.text: First-person experience is unavoidable evidence for any worldview, and its qualitative character is not exhausted merely by cataloguing neural correlations, behavioral functions, or quantitative physical relations.

novelty.explanation: It combines the transcript's correlation limit and qualitative gap into a shared evidential premise.

premises.text: A personal ground has a potential explanatory advantage over an impersonal fundamental property when the phenomena requiring explanation include unified subjects, intentional thought, rational evaluation, and interpersonal understanding.

novelty.explanation: It supplies a comparative reason why divine consciousness might explain more than resemblance alone.

premises.text: Mechanistic explanations of neural organization and evolutionary development can remain complete at their own level while a metaphysical explanation addresses why a consciousness-permitting order and conscious subjects exist.

novelty.explanation: It develops the transcript's complementary-explanation distinction while incorporating evolutionary mechanisms.

premises.text: Theism should not demand an origin for every fundamental posit while exempting God arbitrarily; its claim is instead that a necessary, nonderived personal reality offers greater unification than brute experiential properties.

novelty.explanation: It repairs the regress vulnerability by stating a symmetric explanatory standard and comparative claim.

premises.text: No single consciousness problem establishes theism, but qualitative experience, unified subjecthood, rational agency, and the intelligibility of persons may jointly provide modest abductive support for a personal foundation.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a cumulative abductive structure absent from the participant's individual origin and compatibility claims.

conclusion.text: Accordingly, consciousness can count as limited comparative evidence for a divine personal ground if that hypothesis unifies these features more informatively and economically than non-theistic fundamental-consciousness alternatives.

novelty.explanation: It narrows the conclusion to conditional comparative support and directly answers the nondiscrimination objection.

newArguments.title: Personal Explanatory Fit
newArguments.text: An explanation should be assessed by how naturally its resources match the phenomenon, not solely by counting entities. Conscious subjects possess unified perspectives, intentional states, and capacities for rational relationship. A foundational conscious agent therefore has a kind of structural fit with finite persons that an unspecified intrinsic property lacks. This does not prove divine creation, but it identifies a comparative explanatory virtue: the proposed source already instantiates mentality and agency, while an impersonal panpsychist base needs additional principles connecting rudimentary experience to personal subjecthood.

novelty.explanation: This is a new argument from explanatory fit between personal phenomena and a personal metaphysical foundation.

newArguments.title: Two-Level Explanatory Test
newArguments.text: The divine hypothesis can be evaluated without competing with neuroscience by separating mechanism from metaphysical dependence. Neural and evolutionary theories should predict when consciousness changes and how complex capacities develop; the theistic proposal should explain why such consciousness-bearing laws and unified subjects exist at all. Theism gains support only if it contributes genuine unification at the second level without disrupting the first. This test strengthens the position by making it accountable: scientific success is welcomed, and divine grounding must earn its place through comparative explanatory value rather than through gaps in mechanism.

novelty.explanation: It repairs the compatibility argument by specifying distinct explanatory tasks and a criterion for genuine divine contribution.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that non-theistic panpsychism remains sufficient when it integrates qualitative experience with physical structure, treats combination as an open research burden, and requires independent evidence before adding divine agency.

novelty.explanation: It strengthens the live case by making sufficiency conditional on explicit research and comparative standards.

premises.text: Physical science characterizes relational structure and behavior extraordinarily well, yet those descriptions do not alone settle the intrinsic character of the entities occupying that structure.

novelty.explanation: It preserves the methodological insight while avoiding an excessive claim of permanent scientific incapacity.

premises.text: Identifying intrinsic physical reality with rudimentary experience offers one ontology containing both quantitative relations and qualitative existence, without adding a separately interacting mental substance.

novelty.explanation: It develops the intrinsic-nature proposal into an explicit one-ontology unification claim.

premises.text: Parsimony must compare total commitments, so panpsychism must count its identity and combination principles while theism must count divine attributes, creation relations, and finite-subject dependence.

novelty.explanation: It repairs the transcript's abbreviated entity counting by requiring symmetric total-cost accounting.

premises.text: The combination problem is serious but does not defeat the framework if proposed unity principles become independently constrained by neuroscience, system organization, and empirically distinguishable models of conscious integration.

novelty.explanation: It converts a generic research possibility into a constrained program responsive to the strongest objection.

premises.text: An additional divine consciousness is warranted only if it predicts, unifies, or explains features that fundamental non-theistic consciousness and natural organization cannot address with comparable economy.

novelty.explanation: It develops the denial of inference into a positive evidential standard for adding theism.

conclusion.text: Therefore, non-theistic panpsychism remains a proportionate candidate unless divine grounding demonstrates an independent comparative advantage, while combination remains a substantive problem to investigate rather than evidence for God.

novelty.explanation: It preserves the motion-level conclusion while expressly retaining the combination burden and comparative openness.

newArguments.title: Constraint Convergence
newArguments.text: A productive combination theory should be constrained from several directions at once. Phenomenology identifies unity and differentiation requiring explanation; neuroscience identifies integration, boundaries, and causal organization; metaphysics specifies when many experiential constituents could constitute one subject. A proposal supported independently across these levels would not merely rename emergence. This convergence strategy gives panpsychism a disciplined research path while allowing failure: if no principled mapping between organization and subject unity appears, the framework loses explanatory credibility. The strategy is non-theistic because none of its constraints presupposes a directing mind.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a multi-level constraint methodology for evaluating prospective solutions to the combination problem.

newArguments.title: Explanatory Screening Test
newArguments.text: Before adding God, compare what changes after the divine hypothesis is introduced. If the probabilities of qualitative consciousness, unified subjects, particular psychophysical laws, or evolutionary pathways remain unspecified, divine consciousness may label an ultimate source without increasing explanatory resolution. Panpsychism faces an analogous test for its intrinsic identity and combination rules. Applying the same screening standard to both positions prevents selective demands and clarifies the dispute: whichever framework supplies better constrained expectations with fewer independent assumptions receives the comparative advantage, while mere compatibility or unanswered questions confer little evidential weight.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a symmetric screening test based on changes in explanatory resolution and constrained expectations.
